title: Does private preschool really give children a head start?
summary: In rural India, children in private preschools learn far more than those in public ones. Unequal access to private preschools explains most of the learning gap between richer and poorer children at school entry.

title: Can bank access help farmers weather climate shocks?
summary: India's 1980s rural bank branch expansion only had modest effects on average agricultural output, but it substantially reduced farmers' vulnerability to adverse rainfall shocks, largely by helping them sustain irrigation.

title: Does making formality less costly actually pay off?
summary: By making formalisation cheaper and easier, Brazil’s MEI programme helped millions of microentrepreneurs register – but delivered little in higher earnings, functioning instead as a subsidised expansion of social security access at a net fiscal cost.

title: Why businesses stay small in emerging markets
summary: New research explains why businesses in developing economies remain smaller and grow more slowly than their counterparts in advanced economies – pointing to regulatory hurdles, credit constraints, and measurement challenges as key culprits.

title: Do language barriers hold back agricultural development?

title: Can forecasting social science make experiments better?
summary: Evidence from 100 Social Science Prediction Platform projects shows that research forecasts are too optimistic on average, but still predictive enough to improve study design when they are combined, shrunk, and weighted carefully.
